headline: Public transcriptomic cohorts and ML nominate hub genes across immune-mediated diseases
label: Machine Learning Transcriptomic Biomarker Discovery
summary: Public bulk and single-cell datasets are increasingly paired with multi-ML feature selection, with sphingolipid metabolism emerging as a new axis.
synthesis: The dominant thread is machine learning applied to transcriptomic and multi-omic data to nominate candidate genes, proteins, or pathways in immune-linked and metabolic conditions. Several published entries integrate ML with bioinformatic screening. In periodontitis and systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis, integrative bioinformatics and ML of GEO expression data identify shared genes, with SELP proposed as a diagnostic biomarker supported by docking analysis. In type 2 diabetes and fracture, ML and WGCNA nominate hub genes PLK1, CCNA2 and CHEK1, validated in high-glucose MC3T3-E1 cells. A graph-attention multi-omics model applied to 146 patients nominates hub proteins in breast cancer liver depression syndrome. Not all items share this design: the caloric restriction and adipose metabolomics preprints address lipid and RNA remodeling in mouse brain and obesity-associated adipose tissue. What is new is convergence on sphingolipid metabolism. Single-cell profiling identifies B cell-intrinsic sphingolipid biosynthesis dysregulation in primary immune thrombocytopenia, with UGCG inhibition proposed as an improvement, and transcriptomics-metabolomics in rheumatoid arthritis reveals sphingolipid reprogramming across syndrome differentiation.
